title: Minnesota's 1st Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Minnesota's 1st Congressional District will determine who represents the largely rural, southern Minnesota district stretching from the South Dakota to Wisconsin borders, including Rochester, Mankato, Winona, and Austin. Incumbent Republican Rep. Brad Finstad, first elected in a 2022 special election and re-elected with 58.5% in 2024, is seeking a third full term. The Democratic-Farmer-Labor (DFL) primary features a competitive contest between high school math teacher Jake Johnson, who has drawn national attention and significant fundraising, and Alex Eaton, while Finstad faces Republican primary challengers Greg Goetzman and Oliver Morlan, who is also running as an independent. The race has become more competitive than expected, with polls showing Johnson within striking distance and national analysts shifting the rating from Safe Republican to Likely Republican, making it a potential Democratic pickup opportunity in the fight for House control.
polling_note: Two polls were found. Both show Finstad leading but within a competitive margin, though note the Ragnar Research poll was conducted for a Republican client and the PPP poll for the Johnson campaign. The primaries are scheduled for August 11, 2026, so general election polling currently tests Finstad vs. Johnson as the likely DFL nominee.

candidates.name: Brad Finstad
candidates.summary: Brad Finstad is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Minnesota's 1st Congressional District, first elected in a 2022 special election and re-elected in 2022 and 2024. A fourth-generation farmer from New Ulm, he previously served in the Minnesota House of Representatives (2003–2009) and as Minnesota state director of USDA Rural Development under President Trump (2017–2021). Finstad serves on the House Agriculture, Armed Services, and Small Business committees, and chairs the Agriculture Subcommittee on Nutrition, Foreign Agriculture, and Horticulture.

candidates.name: Jake Johnson
candidates.summary: Jake Johnson is a high school math teacher at Mayo High School in Rochester and a DFL candidate for U.S. House in Minnesota's 1st Congressional District. He grew up in Stewartville in a working-class family of 11 children, attended the University of Wisconsin-La Crosse with the help of Pell Grants, and has taught math for 20 years in Rochester Public Schools. Johnson serves as Governmental Relations Coordinator for his teachers union and has been endorsed by the Minnesota DFL Party, Sen. Tina Smith, former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, and the National Education Association.

candidates.name: Oliver Morlan
candidates.summary: Oliver Morlan is an independent candidate running for Minnesota's 1st Congressional District. A 25-year-old from Zumbro Falls and 2018 graduate of Century High School, he works as an operations supervisor/trainer for D&M Industrial Cleaners, his family's commercial cleaning business. Morlan campaigns on fiscal responsibility, term limits, and an America First agenda, emphasizing centrist values and environmental stewardship.

forecast.rationale: Incumbent Republican Brad Finstad is favored for re-election in this Republican-leaning southern Minnesota district (Trump +7 in 2020; Finstad won 58.5% in 2024) but the race has become genuinely competitive. The two available polls — Ragnar Research (R client, March 2026) showing Finstad +10 and Public Policy Polling (D/Johnson campaign, Feb 2026) showing Finstad +3 — both place Finstad ahead, averaging about a 6–7 point lead, but with a significant spread indicating uncertainty. Challenger Jake Johnson is a credible, well-funded DFL candidate with key endorsements (Buttigieg, Sen. Smith, NEA, state DFL party), and national analysts have shifted the rating from Safe R to Likely R. However, only two partisan-sponsored polls exist, the August 11 primary has yet to occur (general election matchups are not fully settled), and this is a historically Republican district with an incumbent who has consistently outperformed the top of the ticket. Independent candidate Oliver Morlan adds a minor wildcard.
